idiom_name: circe Decoder.instance with downField and getOrElse (generic-extras useDefaults / strictDecoding)
implementation_notes: With circe the reader is a Decoder value rather than a class: a hand-written Decoder.instance navigates with downField("name") and supplies defaults via .as[Option[T]].map(_.getOrElse(default)) or a failed cursor's getOrElse, while semi-automatic derivation already ignores unknown keys (unknown fields are simply never requested; strictDecoding = true is the opt-in opposite) and generic-extras Configuration(useDefaults = true) makes case-class default arguments fill absent fields. play-json models the same thing with `(js \ "field")`, which yields a JsLookupResult to be handled with asOpt or validate.
pitfalls: Derived decoders fail on an absent field unless it has a default and useDefaults is enabled (or the field is Option), so the missing-value half of the pattern must be configured, not assumed.
strictDecoding = true converts every producer addition into a DecodingFailure: enabling it for one integration is a deliberate breaking change and should not be the project default.

circe refuses to decode a non-object into a case class (downField on a null/absent parent yields a failed cursor), so payloads that may be null or a different shape need an explicit fallback at the top level.
